Fit a zero-inflated spatial autoregressive (ZISAR) model

Source: R/zisar.R
zisar.Rd

Fits the ZISAR model of Salvini, Arbia and Nardelli (2026): a zero-inflated negative binomial model whose log-mean follows a simultaneous autoregressive (SAR) process with unit-level random effects. By default the inflation probability depends on covariates only (the restricted model); with zero_spatial = TRUE it has a spatial random field of its own (the general model). zisar() takes a two-part formula and a data frame; zisar_fit() is the matrix interface underneath it.

Usage

zisar(
  formula,
  data,
  W,
  zero_spatial = FALSE,
  fixed = NULL,
  start = NULL,
  logdet = c("auto", "eigen", "sparse"),
  control = list(),
  silent = TRUE
)

zisar_fit(
  y,
  X,
  Z = NULL,
  W,
  offset = NULL,
  zero_spatial = FALSE,
  fixed = NULL,
  start = NULL,
  logdet = c("auto", "eigen", "sparse"),
  control = list(),
  silent = TRUE
)

Arguments

formula

A two-part formula y ~ x1 + x2 | z1 + z2: the terms before | enter the count process, those after it the zero-inflation process. Without |, both processes use the same terms. Use | 1 for a constant inflation probability. An offset() term in the count part enters the log-mean with coefficient one.

data

A data frame with one row per spatial unit, in the order of the rows of W. Missing values are not allowed: every unit enters the spatial multiplier, so none can be dropped.

W

Spatial weights: an \(n \times n\) matrix (base or sparse 'Matrix') or an spdep listw object, with zero diagonal and preferably row-standardised.

zero_spatial

If TRUE, fit the general model, with a SAR random field in the inflation predictor (see Model).

fixed

Optional named list of parameters held at fixed values: rho, kappa, sigma, and in the general model rho0 and sigma0 (scalars, natural scale), beta (length ncol(X)) or gamma (length ncol(Z)). In beta and gamma, NA entries are estimated.

start

Optional named list of starting values, with the same names and scales as fixed. Defaults: beta from a Poisson regression, inflation intercept from the share of zeros, rho = 0, kappa = 1, sigma = 0.5, and rho0 = 0, sigma0 = 0.5.

logdet

Method for the log-determinant: "auto", "eigen" or "sparse". See Estimation.

control

List of control parameters for stats::nlminb(), merged with the defaults eval.max = 1000, iter.max = 500, rel.tol = 1e-10.

silent

If FALSE, print the 'TMB' tracing output.

y

Vector of non-negative integer counts.

X

Design matrix of the count process, \(n \times p\); include a column of ones for an intercept.

Z

Design matrix of the zero-inflation process, \(n \times q\). NULL gives an intercept only.

offset

Optional vector of length \(n\) added to the count log-mean (for example the log of an exposure).

Value

An object of class "zisar", a list with, among others:

coefficients

List with the count (\(\beta\)) and zero (\(\gamma\)) coefficients.

rho, kappa, sigma

Spatial autoregressive parameter, negative binomial shape and random-effect standard deviation.

rho0, sigma0

In the general model, the spatial autoregressive parameter and standard deviation of the inflation field; NULL otherwise.

eta

Mode of the latent field \(\eta\) given the data.

g

Mode of the inflation field \(g\) (zero in the restricted model).

fitted.values

Fitted means \(E[y_i] = (1 - \pi_i)\mu_i\).

loglik

Laplace-approximated marginal log-likelihood.

convergence, message

Convergence code and message of stats::nlminb().

max_grad, laplace_ok

Largest gradient component at the optimum, and whether the optimum passed the checks described in Estimation.

tmb

The 'TMB' object, for advanced use.

Use the methods summary(), coef(), vcov(), logLik(), predict(), residuals() and zisar_effects() rather than the components directly.

Model

For units \(i = 1, \dots, n\) linked by a spatial weights matrix \(W\), $$\eta = \rho W \eta + X\beta + u, \qquad u \sim N(0, \sigma^2 I),$$ so that \(\eta = (I - \rho W)^{-1}(X\beta + u)\). Each count is zero with probability \(\pi_i\) (a structural zero) and otherwise negative binomial, $$y_i \sim \pi_i \, 1\{y_i = 0\} + (1 - \pi_i)\, \mathrm{NB}(\mu_i, \kappa), \qquad \mu_i = \exp(\eta_i + o_i), \qquad \mathrm{logit}(\pi_i) = z_i'\gamma,$$ with \(\mathrm{Var}(y_i \mid \text{not a structural zero}) = \mu_i + \mu_i^2/\kappa\) and \(o_i\) an optional offset (log exposure). The offset scales unit \(i\) only: it does not pass through the spatial multiplier.

In the general model (zero_spatial = TRUE) the inflation predictor has a SAR random field of its own, $$\mathrm{logit}(\pi_i) = z_i'\gamma + g_i, \qquad g = \rho_0 W g + e_0, \qquad e_0 \sim N(0, \sigma_0^2 I),$$ independent of \(u\), so that structural zeros can cluster in space beyond what the covariates explain. The restricted model is the limit \(\sigma_0 \to 0\).

Estimation

The latent field \(\eta\) is integrated out with the Laplace approximation in 'TMB' (together with \(g\) in the general model), and the marginal likelihood is maximised with stats::nlminb() over \((\beta, \gamma, \rho, \kappa, \sigma)\), plus \((\rho_0, \sigma_0)\) in the general model, with \(\rho = \tanh(\rho_{raw})\) restricted to \((-1, 1)\). Standard errors come from the inverse Hessian of the Laplace objective; those of \(\rho\), \(\kappa\), \(\sigma\), \(\rho_0\) and \(\sigma_0\) from the delta method.

The Laplace approximation can break down. For a zero count, the conditional distribution of \(\eta_i\) can be bimodal (a structural zero with a large mean, or a negative binomial zero with a small one), and when \(\sigma\) is large the approximation produces spurious optima with a positive log-likelihood and a huge gradient. This happens mostly with small samples and misspecified models (an omitted covariate inflates \(\sigma\)). Each fit is therefore checked: when the optimiser does not converge, or the optimum has a gradient above 0.01 or a positive log-likelihood, the fit is restarted from three other values of \(\kappa\) and \(\sigma\) and from up to three random perturbations of the best point (this uses the random number generator). If no usable optimum is found, zisar() warns and laplace_ok is FALSE.

The general model is more exposed to this breakdown: a zero count can come from a large \(g_i\) (a structural zero) or from a small \(\eta_i\) (a negative binomial zero), and the two latent fields compete for the same zeros. Fit the restricted model first, and treat a general fit with laplace_ok = FALSE as uninformative about \((\rho_0, \sigma_0)\).

The log-determinant \(\log|I - \rho W|\) is computed either from the eigenvalues of \(W\), found once in \(O(n^3)\) time and \(O(n^2)\) memory (logdet = "eigen"), or from a sparse Cholesky factorisation of \((I - \rho W)'(I - \rho W)\) at each evaluation (logdet = "sparse"), which scales to tens of thousands of units. "auto" uses the sparse method when \(n > 5000\).

Nested models

fixed holds parameters at given values, which gives the special cases of the model: fixed = list(rho = 0) is the aspatial zero-inflated negative binomial with random effects (ZINB-RE), and with an intercept-only inflation part (y ~ x | 1), fixed = list(gamma = -20) sets \(\pi_i \approx 0\), the SAR negative binomial with random effects (SAR-NB-RE). Likelihood-ratio tests between nested fits use logLik(). The restricted model sits on the boundary of the general one (\(\sigma_0 = 0\)), so the likelihood-ratio statistic between them does not have the usual chi-squared distribution: its p-value from \(\chi^2_2\) is conservative.

References

Salvini, N., Arbia, G. and Nardelli, V. (2026). ZISAR: A zero-inflated spatial autoregressive model for count data with random effects. Working paper, Università Cattolica del Sacro Cuore.

Kristensen, K., Nielsen, A., Berg, C. W., Skaug, H. and Bell, B. M. (2016). TMB: Automatic differentiation and Laplace approximation. Journal of Statistical Software, 70(5), 1–21. doi:10.18637/jss.v070.i05

See also

zisar_effects() for direct, indirect and total effects, rzisar() to simulate from the model.

Examples

set.seed(1)
sim <- rzisar(12, beta = c(1, 0.5), rho = 0.4, gamma = c(-1, 0.8))
fit <- zisar(y ~ x1 | z1, data = sim$data, W = sim$W)
summary(fit)
#> 
#> Call:
#> zisar(formula = y ~ x1 | z1, data = sim$data, W = sim$W)
#> 
#> 144 spatial units, 38.9% zeros
#> 
#> Count model coefficients (SAR negative binomial, log link):
#>             Estimate Std. Error z value     Pr(>|z|)    
#> (Intercept)    1.622      0.809    2.01        0.045 *  
#> x1             0.669      0.114    5.87 0.0000000045 ***
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
#> 
#> Zero-inflation model coefficients (binomial, logit link):
#>             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)   
#> (Intercept)   -0.805      0.264   -3.05   0.0023 **
#> z1             0.652      0.224    2.91   0.0037 **
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
#> 
#> Spatial and dispersion parameters:
#>       Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)
#> rho      0.106      0.412    0.26      0.8
#> kappa    1.461      0.803                 
#> sigma    0.203      0.628                 
#> 
#> Log-likelihood (Laplace): -344.3 on 7 Df
#> AIC: 702.61   BIC: 723.39
#> Log-determinant: eigen.  Optimiser: converged after 24 iterations.
#> 

# Aspatial ZINB with random effects, and a likelihood-ratio test of rho = 0
fit0 <- zisar(y ~ x1 | z1, data = sim$data, W = sim$W,
              fixed = list(rho = 0))
lr <- 2 * (logLik(fit) - logLik(fit0))
pchisq(as.numeric(lr), df = 1, lower.tail = FALSE)
#> [1] 0.8091

# \donttest{
# General model: zeros clustered by a spatial field of their own
set.seed(2)
sim2 <- rzisar(15, beta = c(1, 0.5), rho = 0.4, gamma = c(-1, 0.8),
               rho0 = 0.6, sigma0 = 1)
fit2 <- zisar(y ~ x1 | z1, data = sim2$data, W = sim2$W,
              zero_spatial = TRUE)
summary(fit2)
